raw:
{
  "need": "Autonomy",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "note": "Each reset feels like proof they can't be trusted, which stings harder than the rule itself." },
  "read": "They're not blowing off curfew to be defiant — they're testing how much control they have over their own life. Every excuse is a bid to keep expanding that boundary on their terms. The repeated resets have turned this into a power negotiation, and their status is quietly on the line every time they come home and face the conversation.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lock it down hard — earlier curfew, immediate consequence, no more discussion — which signals distrust and makes them dig in deeper just to prove a point." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the curfew firm as a non-negotiable standard, but hand them real agency inside it: they help set the terms, they track their own record, and they earn expansion through demonstrated follow-through rather than arguing for it.",
  "holdFirm": ["There is a curfew. That is not on the table.", "Slipping it or excusing it after the fact is not an option we keep resetting indefinitely."],
  "stayFlexible": ["They get genuine input on what the time actually is — within reason.", "The path to a later curfew is a clean track record, not a better argument.", "How they check in can flex — text, call, whatever works — as long as it happens."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 4, "label": "Choices" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I'm not coming at you angry right now. I want to actually sort this out because three resets in and we're still circling the same problem, which tells me something isn't working for either of us." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Tell me honestly — what keeps happening? Is the time just wrong, is it the situation you're in when it's time to leave, or something else? Because I'd rather understand it than just keep having this same fight." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here's what I'm willing to do: let's set a time together right now, one you actually think is realistic, and I'll take that seriously. But I need you to take the other side seriously too — that means no slipping it, no texts after the fact saying you're running late. If something genuine comes up, you call before, not after. You want more trust from me, this is exactly how you build it." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I'm holding you to this because I think you're ready to actually own it — not because I want to control your Friday nights, but because I have a high standard for how you follow through on your word, and I genuinely believe you can meet it. A month of clean runs and we revisit the time. That's a real path forward. What's the time you're proposing?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "The curfew is almost never really about the hour — it's about whether they get to be someone who earns trust or someone who gets managed. Keep the follow-through visible and tied explicitly to expanding freedom, so they experience responsibility as the thing that gets them more of what they want, not less."
}
situation: Curfew keeps slipping later and the excuses pile up. We have already reset it twice.
